title: Effects of light transitions on measures of alertness, arousal and comfort
classification_signals: Results tables with statistical tests (t-tests, contrast analyses)

filename_mismatch.inventory_filename: De Prado Bert et al. - 2018 - The Effects of Air Pollution on the Brain a Review of Studies Interfacing Environmental Epidemiolog.pdf
filename_mismatch.actual_paper: Kompier et al. 2020 - Effects of light transitions on measures of alertness, arousal and comfort

research_question: How do abrupt light transitions (onset, persistence, and symmetry) affect subjective experiences (alertness, arousal, comfort) and objective physiological measures (skin conductance, heart rate, skin temperature) in humans, and what are the underlying mechanisms?

hypotheses.statement: Light transitions from warm dim to cool bright will increase alertness and arousal compared to constant lighting conditions
Thermal responses will be affected by light transitions, with cool bright light producing warmer perception due to coolness associations
Comfort ratings will show transition effects with cool bright light producing immediate changes

findings.antecedent: Abrupt transition from warm dim light (WD, ~26 lux, CCT 3000K) to cool bright light (CB, ~901 lux, CCT 5000K)
findings.consequent: Sensation of Light Intensity (subjective brightness perception on 9-point scale)

instruments_used.name: 9-point Likert scale for Light Intensity Sensation

scope_conditions.population: healthy adults (N=38, 19 female, mean age 24.3 years)
scope_conditions.duration: acute (45-min experimental session with 15-min measurement blocks)

findings.mechanism: Cool bright light contains higher short-wavelength radiation which increases perceived brightness, and higher illuminance (901 lux vs 26 lux) provides more sensory input

mechanism_chain.to_construct: increased short-wavelength photon exposure and higher illuminance
enhanced retinal signal to visual system
increased perception of brightness

theory_commitments.specific_claim: rapid changes in illuminance and color temperature are detected immediately by the visual system, supporting model of fast visual transduction
